answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: treat trust as a conserved flow, not a cloneable label. Each marble anchor emits a bounded quantity of trust, and standing is the max-flow reaching an identity from anchors through the vouching graph. Because flow is conserved, the total trust a sybil region can draw is capped by the capacity of the cut to the honest core, however many fakes crowd behind it. A thousand clones in a lagoon split one thin inflow, each a sliver. An attacker cannot mint trust by minting identities, only by widening the cut: earning real edges from anchors that watch like a falcon.
